description: A 40x40 red panel with a 20x20 backdrop-filter: brightness(0.5) glass centered over it and no own background -- proves the glass darkens whatever is already painted behind it rather than painting its own content.

florui.css: .group { display: grid; grid-template-columns: 40px; grid-template-rows: 40px; width: 40px; height: 40px; } .group .back { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; width: 40px; height: 40px; background-color: #ff0000; } .group .glass { grid-column: 1; grid-row: 1; width: 20px; height: 20px; margin-top: 10px; margin-left: 10px; backdrop-filter: brightness(0.5); }

classification.reason: Measured directly against a real Chromium capture: 6.25% of pixels differ by exactly 1 of 255 color levels (max_error 1), the same rounding-mode signature already calibrated for filter-adjustments -- not a wrong formula, which would show a large uniform error.
